newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends up, gilt prices down in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: India call ends up, gilt prices down in thin trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday at 9.75-10.5 percent, up from Tuesday's close of 4.5 percent on reduced fund supply following a bond sale by the central bank, dealers said.
They said there was good demand for 12.59 percent 2004 government of India bond, put up for sale by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) earlier in the day.
The RBI said it accepted bids for 46.86 billion rupees at the sale.
Dealers said most of the day's trade in call money was between 8.5 percent and 10.0 percent, with some stray deals at 10.5 percent.
Some dealers said they expected call money to drop to around 7.0-8.0 percent on Thursday and ease further to 5.0-6.0 percent by the end of the week.

"The uncertainty over quantum of funds outflow towards the bond sale is over," said a dealer. "This will help stabilise the market. Further about 51 billion rupees come back to banks on Saturday when the RBI reverses a repo held on June 23."
Prices of government securities fell in light trade as market players awaited details of the bond sale, dealers said.

"Prices fell as there was a realignment on the new price," said Felix D'Cunha, dealer at Tower Capital. "The RBI chose to sell the stock at par against its prevailing price of 101.4 rupees. This type of action tends to distort the yield curve."
The 12.59 percent 2004 stock traded at par on Wednesday against 100.13 rupees on Tuesday, the 12.14 percent 2000 fell to 100.7 from 101.2 and the 13.05 percent 2007 to 102.4 from 103, dealers said.
